subtopic: The Argand Plane and Polar Representation
title: Worked: all four quadrants at once

board_content.text: Find modulus and principal argument of each of $\pm 1\pm i\sqrt3$.
All four share $r=2$ and reference angle $\tfrac{\pi}{3}$; only the quadrant differs.
Quadrants III and IV give negative principal arguments.
This single problem drills every row of the quadrant table.

segments_english.text: This one example exercises the entire quadrant table at once, so it's worth doing carefully.
Find the modulus and principal argument of all four numbers plus or minus one, plus or minus i root three.
Every one of them has the same modulus: root of one plus three, which is two. And every one has the same reference angle: inverse tangent of root three, which is pi over three.

Now the quadrants. One plus i root three is in quadrant one, so its argument is pi over three. Minus one plus i root three is in quadrant two, so its argument is pi minus pi over three, which is two pi over three.

Minus one minus i root three is in quadrant three, giving alpha minus pi, that is minus two pi over three. And one minus i root three is in quadrant four, giving minus alpha, which is minus pi over three.
So all four have modulus two and reference angle pi over three. The only thing that changed across the four was the quadrant.
Notice that quadrants three and four produce negative principal arguments, because the point sits below the real axis, and the principal range dips into the negatives there.
If you can do this one problem cleanly, you have effectively drilled every row of the quadrant table in a single stroke.

segments_hinglish.text: Ye ek example poore quadrant table ko ek saath exercise karta hai, to ise dhyaan se karna worth hai.
Chaaron numbers plus or minus one, plus or minus i root three ke modulus aur principal argument nikaalo.
In sab ka modulus same hai: root of one plus three, jo hai two. Aur sab ka reference angle same hai: inverse tangent of root three, jo hai pi over three.

Ab quadrants. One plus i root three quadrant one mein hai, to iska argument pi over three. Minus one plus i root three quadrant two mein hai, to iska argument pi minus pi over three, jo hai two pi over three.

Minus one minus i root three quadrant three mein hai, deta hai alpha minus pi, yaani minus two pi over three. Aur one minus i root three quadrant four mein hai, deta hai minus alpha, jo hai minus pi over three.
To chaaron ka modulus two aur reference angle pi over three. Chaaron mein sirf quadrant badla.
Dhyaan do ki quadrant three aur four negative principal arguments dete hain, kyunki point real axis ke neeche baithta hai, aur principal range wahan negatives mein dip karti hai.
Agar aap ye ek problem cleanly kar lo, to aapne effectively poore quadrant table ki har row ek hi stroke mein drill kar li.
